title: Will Autonomous AI Agents Replace Developers?

scenes.title: The Billion Dollar Debate
scenes.prompt: Futuristic neon-lit tech debate stage with high-tech hologram screens and microphones

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: By 2026, over 40 percent of all commercial code is written by autonomous agents. But tonight, two industry leaders clash over what happens next.

dialogue.speaker: host
dialogue.text: Dr. Vance, founders are bragging on Twitter that they fired their entire junior engineering team. Are programmers actually obsolete?

dialogue.speaker: guest
dialogue.text: Absolutely not, Alex. Agents generate syntax fast, but they don't understand architecture, edge cases, or catastrophic security failures. You aren't replacing engineers, you are turning them into system directors.

scenes.title: The Economic Shift
scenes.prompt: Split screen showing automated server terminal on left and a focused software architect on right

dialogue.speaker: host
dialogue.text: Yet solo developers are building million dollar SaaS businesses in days without hiring a team. Isn't that real disruption?

dialogue.speaker: guest
dialogue.text: It is real leverage, not magic. The engineers who win in this economy are the ones who master orchestration, verification, and problem framing.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: The tools have changed forever, but the architects who command them will rule the next decade.
